subject: mathematics
question_text: Find a unit vector perpendicular to the plane determined by the points P(1, −1, 2), Q(2, 0, −1) and R(0, 2, −1).

verification.note: Source: Baby Bullet-Q, Junior Inter Maths-1A (Sri Publishers, Machilipatnam), book p.105 — from the book's separate "STAR QUESTIONS PLUS" bank, answer 160. That bank (book pp.98-111, answers 142-180) sits AFTER all the numbered chapters and is organised by chapter rather than forming part of any chapter's own inventory; it is authored into this unit because that is where the question belongs on the paper (founder decision 2026-08-22). SECTION: classed SAQ on its length and shape. The bank prints no mark cut, so this classification is OURS — the same shape as Unit 5's own SAQ answer 59. Printed appearances: none — this answer carries no year tag. Three POINTS, not vectors — so two edge vectors have to be built first. The ± in the answer is required: a plane has two unit normals, one on each side. ⚠ THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S — the bank prints no [N Marks] tags anywhere. The shapes used follow the splits the book DOES print elsewhere: 1+1 for a 2-mark VSAQ (answers 100, 101 on book p.82), 1+1+1+1 or 1+2+1 for a 4-mark SAQ (answers 58, 59 on p.63 and 61 on p.64), and the granular split for a 7-mark LAQ (answer 32 on p.44). This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

recall_prompt: Say how you would do this one — name each move in order.

steps.label: Build two edge vectors
steps.margin_note: First mark. Subtract the position vector of P from the other two to get PQ and PR — both lie in the plane.
lines: OP = i − j + 2k, OQ = 2i − k, OR = 2j + k

recall.must_convey: That PQ = i + j − 3k and PR = −i + 3j − k are formed by subtracting OP.
accept: subtract O P from O Q and O R to get the two edge vectors
P Q is i plus j minus three k and P R is minus i plus three j minus k
build two vectors that lie in the plane first
O P teesi rendu edge vectors ravali
form P Q and P R

steps.why: A cross product needs vectors, and the question gives points. Both edges must start at the SAME point, or they will not span the plane.
common_mistakes: Crossing the position vectors OP and OQ directly.
Building PQ from P and QR from Q, which do not share a starting point.

steps.label: Find PQ × PR
steps.margin_note: Half the marks. The cross product of two vectors in the plane is perpendicular to the plane. Factor out the common 4 — it makes the next step much lighter.

accept: the cross product is eight i plus four j plus four k which is four times two i plus j plus k
take the common factor four out of the cross product
the normal vector is four times two i plus j plus k
cross product lo four common teeyali
compute P Q cross P R
heard_as: two i plus j plus k

steps.why: Factoring out the 4 does not change the direction, and the magnitude that follows is far easier to compute from (2, 1, 1) than from (8, 4, 4).
common_mistakes: Sign slip on the j term.
Skipping the common factor and squaring 8, 4, 4.

steps.label: Divide by the magnitude
steps.margin_note: Last mark. A unit vector is the vector over its own length, and BOTH signs are correct answers — write the ±.

recall.must_convey: That dividing by the magnitude 4√6 gives ± (2i + j + k)/√6, with both signs.
accept: divide by four root six to get plus or minus two i plus j plus k over root six
the unit vector is plus or minus that vector over root six
both signs are valid because a plane has two normals
plus or minus rendu correct, root six tho divide cheyyali
the answer is plus or minus two i plus j plus k by root six

steps.why: A plane has two sides, so there are two unit normals pointing opposite ways. Dropping the ± reports only one of two correct answers.
